claim: On Jan. 7, 1610 Galileo saw three points of light by Jupiter; by Jan. 15 he concluded they were four moons orbiting it.

beats.caption: Three stars. Then they moved.
beats.vo: Three tiny stars. Then they moved.

beats.caption: Jan. 7, 1610
beats.vo: On January 7th, 1610, Galileo aimed his improved, homemade, twenty-power telescope at Jupiter.

beats.caption: Distant stars?
beats.vo: Beside the planet sat three points of light. He took them for distant stars.

beats.caption: They moved
beats.vo: But over several nights, they changed places, yet never left Jupiter's side.

beats.caption: A fourth one
beats.vo: Four days later, a fourth point of light joined them, and it behaved the same way.

beats.caption: Four moons
beats.vo: By January fifteenth, Galileo was sure: four moons, circling Jupiter. Strong evidence that not everything circled Earth.
